terms.definition: An energy resource that is being (or can be) replenished as it is used, such as solar, wind, hydroelectricity, tides, waves, geothermal and bio-fuel.
terms.examiner: Some are unreliable: wind and solar depend on weather.

terms.definition: A resource that will run out, such as fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas) and nuclear fuel.
terms.examiner: Reliable, but fossil fuels release carbon dioxide.

terms.definition: A fuel from plant or animal matter; it is renewable and close to carbon neutral.
terms.examiner: Land for crops is a disadvantage.

terms.definition: Fossil fuels release carbon dioxide (global warming) and sulfur dioxide (acid rain); nuclear produces radioactive waste.
terms.examiner: Questions often ask you to weigh up reliability, cost and impact.
